nodes.description: Cells expressing the variant thrombopoietin secrete less of it, and patients have a serum thrombopoietin level lower than expected for their platelet count. In mice, heterozygous loss of Thpo lowers circulating thrombopoietin in proportion to gene dosage, because the gene is constitutively expressed and the level is set by the platelet mass rather than by transcriptional feedback. The authors of the defining report caution that the cell-line trafficking findings may not transfer exactly to endogenous production in patients.

evidence.snippet: A gene dosage effect observed in heterozygous mice suggests that the TPO gene is constitutively expressed and that the circulating TPO level is directly regulated by the platelet mass.

nodes.description: Thrombopoietin acting through MPL is the main regulator of the proliferation and differentiation of hematopoietic progenitors into megakaryocytes. Less circulating thrombopoietin means less MPL signaling in megakaryocyte progenitors. In THC9 the reduction is mild enough that other lineages are spared, unlike biallelic THPO loss.

nodes.description: Homozygous knockouts lose more than 80% of platelets and megakaryocytes with other lineages normal in blood; heterozygotes show a gene dosage effect on circulating thrombopoietin. Knockouts also have fewer myeloid, erythroid and multilineage progenitors in the marrow.
Mild, lifelong reduction of the platelet count, about 100 to 145 x 10^9/L in the defining cohort; some carriers have normal counts.

nodes.description: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists replace the missing ligand at MPL and are the mechanistically matched therapy for THPO-related thrombocytopenia. All reported responses are in biallelic THPO disease (romiplostim, eltrombopag); no treated patient with monoallelic THC9 has been reported, and the mild phenotype rarely calls for treatment.

evidence.reference_title: Thrombopoietin receptor agonists in hereditary thrombocytopenias.
evidence.snippet: We believe that TPO-RAs will play a major role in the treatment of HTPs, particularly myosin heavy chain 9-related disease, Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome, X-linked thrombocytopenia, and thrombocytopenia caused by THPO mutations.

evidence.reference_title: Thrombopoietin mutation in congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia treatable with romiplostim.
evidence.snippet: In all the three affected children, treatment with the THPO-mimetic romiplostim induced trilineage hematological responses, remission of bleeding and infections, and transfusion independence
